definition_zh: 羔羊；小羊；羔羊肉；温顺的人
definition_en: a young sheep; its meat as food; a gentle or innocent person; a religious image of sacrifice
core_image: 刚出生不久的小羊贴在母羊身边，毛还湿着
scene: 清晨的羊圈里，一只小羊跟在母羊身后，叫声又轻又软。 The lamb pressed close to its mother as the farmer opened the gate.
sceneCN: 这里是「羔羊、小羊」（第 1 个义项：年幼的羊）；句意是农夫打开栅栏时，小羊紧紧贴着母羊。图中可辨识物件：羊圈木门、母羊、草垛。

pos.zh: 羔羊；小羊；羔羊肉；温顺的人

derivatives.zh: 由 lamb 加 -ing 构成，义为「产羔；产羔期」
由 lamb 与 skin 复合而成，义为「羔羊皮」
由 lamb 与 like 复合而成，义为「温顺如羔羊的」

senses.title: A young sheep
senses.definition: a young sheep, especially one that is less than a year old
senses.definitionCN: 年幼的羊，尤指不满一岁的小羊
senses.example: The lamb stayed close to its mother in the cold wind.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风里，小羊紧紧贴着母羊。
senses.why: The word has named the young sheep since Old English, and that animal is still the sense people picture first.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从古英语起就指年幼的羊，而这只动物仍是人们最先想到的义项。

senses.title: The meat of a young sheep
senses.definition: the meat of a young sheep, used as food
senses.definitionCN: 幼羊的肉，供人食用
senses.example: We had roast lamb with potatoes on Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 星期天我们吃了烤羔羊肉配土豆。
senses.why: Once an animal is farmed for food, its name easily moves from the living creature to the meat on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 一种动物被饲养供食之后，它的名字很容易从活着的动物转到盘子里的肉。

senses.title: A gentle or innocent person
senses.definition: a meek, innocent or easily led person, often with a touch of irony
senses.definitionCN: 温顺、天真或容易被人牵着走的人，常带一点讽刺
senses.example: He followed her advice like a lamb.
senses.exampleCN: 他像小羊一样乖乖听了她的建议。
senses.why: A lamb is proverbially meek, so the animal's docility is transferred to a person who offers no resistance.
senses.whyCN: 小羊向来被视为温顺，于是这种驯顺被转用到毫不反抗的人身上。

senses.title: A religious image of sacrifice
senses.definition: a lamb used as a religious image of innocence or sacrifice, especially in Christian tradition
senses.definitionCN: 宗教中象征纯洁或祭献的羔羊，尤见于基督教传统
senses.example: The choir sang about the Lamb of God.
senses.exampleCN: 唱诗班唱起了关于上帝羔羊的歌。
senses.why: In biblical language a lamb offered in sacrifice became a picture of innocence given up for others, which fixed this symbolic sense in English.
senses.whyCN: 在圣经语言里，献祭的羔羊成了为他人舍去纯洁的象征，这个象征义因此在英语中固定下来。

intro.en: Lamb is a Germanic word for the young sheep; it never had a Latin twin, and English added meat, character and religious meanings to it.
intro.cn: lamb 是日耳曼语中指小羊的词，从未有拉丁语同形词，英语又给它添上肉食、性格与宗教含义。

items.en: A very old root is often reconstructed behind the word, but its exact form is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个词背后常被重构出一个非常古老的词根，但确切形式并不确定。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed as lambaz, naming a young sheep.
items.cn: 日耳曼语形式通常重构为 lambaz，指年幼的羊。

items.en: Old English lamb already meant a young sheep and appears in early farming and religious texts.
items.cn: 古英语 lamb 已指小羊，见于早期农事与宗教文本。

items.en: Middle English kept lamb unchanged, and the plural lambs settled into the regular English pattern.
items.cn: 中古英语沿用 lamb 的拼写，复数 lambs 也固定为规则形式。

items.en: Modern English uses lamb for the animal, its meat, a meek person and a religious image.
items.cn: 现代英语用 lamb 指小羊、羔羊肉、温顺的人和宗教意象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built from lamb and one accidental spelling neighbour; the near-meaning group gathers other sheep words.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lamb 构成的词和一个只是拼写相邻的词；近义组收其他与羊有关的词。

entries.definition: The skin of a lamb, used for leather or parchment.
entries.definitionCN: 羔羊的皮，可做皮革或羊皮纸。

entries.definition: The season or process of a ewe giving birth to lambs.
entries.definitionCN: 母羊产羔的季节或过程。

entries.definition: Gentle and docile in the way of a lamb.
entries.definitionCN: 像小羊一样温顺驯良的。

entries.definition: Of light or flame: soft and lightly dancing; only the spelling is close, with a different Latin history.
entries.definitionCN: 指光或火焰柔和而轻轻跳动；只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: The adult animal kept for wool and meat.
entries.definitionCN: 为取毛和肉而饲养的成年羊。

entries.definition: A female sheep, especially one old enough to breed.
entries.definitionCN: 母羊，尤指已到繁殖年龄的母羊。

entries.definition: A male sheep, often with large curled horns.
entries.definitionCN: 公羊，常长有大而卷曲的角。

normalIntro.en: The word stays close to the farm; its family adds the season of birth, the skin and the quality of meekness.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词始终贴近农事；它的词族添上产羔季节、羊皮和温顺的性质。

normal.en: Old English lamb is one of the oldest farming words in English, so the animal sense comes before every metaphor.
normal.cn: 古英语 lamb 是英语中最古老的农事词之一，所以动物义先于所有比喻义。

normal.en: The plural is lambs, not lambes, because the word ends in a plain voiced sound rather than a hissing one.
normal.cn: 复数是 lambs 而不是 lambes，因为词尾是普通的浊音，而不是嘶嘶的咝音。

normal.en: Lambing names the season when ewes give birth, which is why the suffix -ing here means a period of activity.
normal.cn: lambing 指母羊生产的季节，所以这里的后缀 -ing 表示一段活动时期。

normal.en: Lambskin is simply lamb plus skin, and it names the hide rather than the living animal.
normal.cn: lambskin 就是 lamb 加 skin，指的是皮张而不是活着的动物。

normal.en: Like a lamb is the phrase that carries the meekness sense, and it often sounds gently ironic.
normal.cn: like a lamb 是承载温顺义的短语，听起来常带一点温和的讽刺。

abstract.en: An animal born helpless becomes a picture of innocence, and from there a picture of sacrifice.
abstract.cn: 一种生来无助的动物先成为纯洁的图画，再由此成为牺牲的图画。

abstract.en: The same word can name a living creature, a meal and a person's character, because farming binds all three together.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能指活物、餐食和人的性格，因为农事把这三者绑在一起。

abstract.en: Lamb shows how a plain farm word can carry a whole moral vocabulary without ever leaving the pen.
abstract.cn: lamb 说明一个朴素的农事词可以承载整套道德语汇，却始终没有离开羊圈。

examples.en: The lamb stayed close to its mother in the cold wind.
examples.cn: 冷风里，小羊紧紧贴着母羊。

examples.en: We had roast lamb with potatoes on Sunday.
examples.cn: 星期天我们吃了烤羔羊肉配土豆。

examples.en: He followed her advice like a lamb.
examples.cn: 他像小羊一样乖乖听了她的建议。

root: 古英语 lamb，源自日耳曼语 lambaz，与荷兰语 lam、德语 Lamm 同族；没有可靠的拉丁语同源词。

sensesIntro.en: The young sheep is the core; the senses divide into its meat, a meek person, and the religious lamb of sacrifice.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是年幼的羊；义项由此分出它的肉、温顺的人，以及宗教中献祭的羔羊。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newborn lamb standing close against its mother's flank.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚出生的小羊紧紧靠在本羊的腹侧。

branches.en: a newborn animal wobbling on its first legs
branches.cn: 刚出生的小羊在初生的腿上摇晃

branches.en: a farm where some animals are kept and some are sold
branches.cn: 既留养一些羊又卖掉一些羊的农场

branches.en: a Sunday table with roast meat and potatoes
branches.cn: 星期天摆着烤肉和土豆的餐桌

branches.en: a person who never says no
branches.cn: 一个从不说「不」的人

branches.en: an altar where innocence is offered up
branches.cn: 献上纯洁的祭坛

intro.cn: 这个日耳曼语名词靠一个后缀表示产羔季节，靠两个复合词表示皮张与性格。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 液体的；液态的；流动而清澈的；（资产）易变现的；现金充裕的
definition_en: in the state of a substance that flows freely, clear and smooth, or easily converted into cash
core_image: 一只玻璃杯里水沿杯壁滑下，杯底的硬币清晰可见
scene: 孩子把杯子打翻，水沿着桌沿流下，滴在地板上。 The child knocked the cup over and the liquid ran along the table edge onto the floor.
sceneCN: 这里指「能自由流动的液体」（第 1 个义项：有一定体积而无固定形状、可流动的物质状态）；句意为孩子打翻杯子，液体沿桌沿流下，滴到地板上。可辨识物件：玻璃杯、桌沿、水滴、地板；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 液体的；液态的；清澈流动的；（资产）易变现的

derivatives.zh: 基础形容词加名词后缀，表性质 → 流动性
基础词干加使动后缀 → 使液化
由该动词加名词后缀 → 液化
基础形容词加动词后缀，义为「使结清」→ 清算；变现
与基础词同出拉丁「流体」的旁系同源词 → 酒；液体

senses.title: A substance that flows freely
senses.titleCN: 能自由流动的物质状态
senses.definition: matter with a definite volume but no fixed shape, which takes the shape of its container
senses.definitionCN: 有一定体积而无固定形状、随容器改变形状的物质
senses.example: Mercury is the only metal that is liquid at room temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 汞是室温下唯一呈液态的金属。
senses.why: the adjective describes the state itself, and the noun names any substance in it, so the pair covers water, oil and melted metal.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述这一状态本身，名词指处于该状态的任何物质，因此水、油与熔化的金属都包括在内。

senses.title: Clear and translucent, as light or eyes
senses.titleCN: 清澈透亮的，如光或眼睛
senses.definition: describing something that lets light through and looks deep rather than cloudy
senses.definitionCN: 描述透光、显得深澈而不浑浊之物
senses.example: The lake was liquid green in the early sun.
senses.exampleCN: 清晨阳光下，湖面泛着清澈的绿。
senses.why: clear water was the original sight behind the word, and the quality was transferred to anything that seems to hold light within.
senses.whyCN: 清水是这个词背后的原始景象，这一性质随后被移到任何仿佛内含光亮之物上。

senses.title: Smooth and flowing in movement or sound
senses.titleCN: 动作或声音的流畅圆润
senses.definition: describing motion or music that runs without jerks, like a stream
senses.definitionCN: 描述动作或音乐毫无顿挫、如水般流淌
senses.example: Her liquid phrasing made the sonata seem easy.
senses.exampleCN: 她流畅的乐句让这首奏鸣曲显得轻松。
senses.why: what flows without obstruction is pleasant to watch or hear, so the physical idea became a word of praise for grace.
senses.whyCN: 无阻流动之物看着听着都舒服，物理观念于是变成赞美优雅的词。

senses.title: Easily turned into cash
senses.definition: describing an asset that can be sold quickly without a loss
senses.definitionCN: 描述能迅速售出而不损失价值的资产
senses.example: Treasury bills are the most liquid asset in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 短期国库券是市场上最容易变现的资产。
senses.why: cash itself flows, so an asset that becomes cash at once is described with the same word as water.
senses.whyCN: 现金本身会流动，能立刻变成现金的资产便与水共用同一个词。

senses.title: A market with many ready buyers
senses.definition: describing a market where large orders are absorbed without moving the price much
senses.definitionCN: 描述能吸收大额订单而价格变动不大的市场
senses.example: The shares became liquid only after the index inclusion.
senses.exampleCN: 这些股票被纳入指数之后才变得易于成交。
senses.why: a market is liquid when orders wait on both sides, so a seller meets a buyer instead of waiting.
senses.whyCN: 市场两侧都挂着订单时才算易成交，卖方能直接遇到买方而不必等待。

senses.title: Cash and near-cash funds
senses.definition: describing money held in cash or in instruments that can be spent almost at once
senses.definitionCN: 描述以现金或几乎可即刻支用的票据持有的钱
senses.example: The firm kept half its wealth in liquid form.
senses.exampleCN: 这家企业把一半财富以现金形式持有。
senses.why: wealth kept as cash can be spent without selling anything, which is the financial form of the same flow.
senses.whyCN: 以现金持有的财富无需出售任何东西就能支用，这是同一流动在金融上的形态。

senses.title: A liquid consonant in phonetics
senses.definition: describing the sounds l and r, which flow into neighbouring sounds without friction
senses.definitionCN: 描述边音与颤音这类与相邻音平滑相接、不产生摩擦的音
senses.example: English has two liquid consonants in most analyses.
senses.exampleCN: 多数分析认为英语有两个流音。
senses.why: phonetics borrowed the flowing image because these sounds pass into their neighbours without a stop, unlike plosives.
senses.whyCN: 语音学借用「流动」意象，因为这些音与邻音相接而不阻塞，与爆破音不同。

senses.title: A liquid diet in medicine
senses.definition: describing food taken as fluids for a period, often after surgery or during illness
senses.definitionCN: 描述在术后或病中一段时间内以流体形式进食
senses.example: He was on a liquid diet for three days.
senses.exampleCN: 他吃了三天流食。
senses.why: the medical use narrows the adjective to what can be swallowed as fluid, which is the oldest physical sense applied to care.
senses.whyCN: 医学用法把这个形容词收窄到可以以流质吞下的食物，这是最古老的物理义被用在照护上。

senses.title: Fluid, unsettled conditions in society
senses.titleCN: 社会中流动不定的状态
senses.definition: describing social or economic arrangements that change constantly and have no fixed form
senses.definitionCN: 描述不断变化、没有固定形态的社会或经济安排
senses.example: Bauman described modern life as liquid because nothing keeps its shape for long.
senses.exampleCN: 鲍曼把现代生活称作液态的，因为没有东西能长久保持形状。
senses.why: the metaphor extends flow from matter to institutions: what is liquid cannot be grasped and held, only followed.
senses.whyCN: 这一隐喻把流动从物质扩展到制度：液态之物抓不住、握不牢，只能跟随。

intro.en: Liquid comes from Latin liquidus 'fluid, clear', from liquere 'to be fluid'. English took it in the fourteenth century as both adjective and noun. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: liquid 来自拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」，其动词为 liquere「呈液态」。英语于 14 世纪把它同时吸收为形容词与名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Liquere meant 'to be fluid, to flow, to be clear'. Its earlier origin is uncertain, and the common reconstruction is a hypothesis rather than a proved form.
items.cn: liquere 意为「呈液态、流动、清澈」。其更早来源不确定，常见重构只是假说，并非已证形式。

items.en: Liquidus described water, oil and melted substances, and also clear light and a smooth style of speech.
items.cn: liquidus 描述水、油与熔化物，也用于清澈的光与平顺的言辞。

items.en: English liquid appears in the fourteenth century, at first for flowing matter; the noun and the adjective developed together.
items.cn: 英语 liquid 于 14 世纪出现，最初指流动的物质；名词与形容词同时发展。

items.en: Seventeenth-century grammars used liquid for sounds that flow into their neighbours, a technical borrowing of the water image.
items.cn: 17 世纪的语法学用 liquid 指流进邻音的音，这是对水的意象的技术性借用。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the adjective was applied to assets that turn into cash quickly, and liquid assets became a standard phrase.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪，这个形容词被用于能迅速变成现金的资产，「流动资产」成为标准说法。

items.en: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries extended it to social arrangements that will not hold their shape, as in liquid modernity.
items.cn: 20 与 21 世纪把它扩展到无法保持形状的社会安排，如「液态现代性」。

note.en: Group one holds words from the flowing root or close in shape; group two holds adjectives that describe fluids, clarity or easy sale.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「流动」词根或形近的词；第二组是描述流体、清澈或易售的其他形容词。

entries.definition: The ease of turning assets into cash; liquid is the adjective that carries the same idea.
entries.definitionCN: 指资产变现的容易程度；liquid 是承载同一观念的形容词。

entries.definition: A distilled alcoholic drink, from Latin liquor 'fluid'; the modern sense is a narrow survival.
entries.definitionCN: 指蒸馏酒，来自拉丁 liquor「流体」；现代义是狭窄的存留。

entries.definition: To sell off assets or wind up a firm; it names the action that makes a holding liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 指出售资产或结束企业；它指使持有物变现的动作。

entries.definition: To make something fluid; it is about physical state, not money.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物液化；关乎物理状态，而非金钱。

entries.definition: A substance that flows; it is the everyday term, while liquid is the technical state between solid and gas.
entries.definitionCN: 指流动的物质；它是日常说法，liquid 是固气之间的技术状态。

entries.definition: Easy to see through; it covers the translucent sense but says nothing about flow or cash.
entries.definitionCN: 指容易看透；只覆盖清澈义，与流动或现金无关。

entries.definition: Free from bumps; it covers the flowing-motion sense but not the substance.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有凹凸；覆盖流畅义，但不指物质状态。

entries.definition: Able to find a buyer; liquid adds that the sale is fast and does not move the price.
entries.definitionCN: 指能寻得买家；liquid 另含「卖得快且不压价」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Water is the original picture: it flows, it is clear, and it takes the shape of whatever holds it.
normal.cn: 水是原始图景：会流、清澈，并随容器改变形状。

normal.en: The family runs liquid, liquidity, liquefy, liquefaction, liquidate, liquor.
normal.cn: 同族词包括液体的、流动性、液化、液化过程、清算、蒸馏酒。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the uses: liquid assets, liquid nitrogen, liquid crystal, liquid diet.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出用法：流动资产、液氮、液晶、流食。

normal.en: In finance the test is simple: can it become cash this week without a discount?
normal.cn: 金融上的检验很简单：它这周能不能不折价地变成现金？

normal.en: In phonetics the same word names sounds that glide into their neighbours.
normal.cn: 在语音学中，同一个词指滑入邻音的那些音。

abstract.en: Picture water sliding down the inside of a glass while a coin at the bottom stays visible.
abstract.cn: 想象水沿杯壁滑下，杯底的硬币仍清晰可见。

abstract.en: Picture a stream that takes the shape of every stone it passes.
abstract.cn: 想象一条溪流，随经过的每块石头改变形状。

abstract.en: Picture a city where the buildings are replaced before anyone learns their names.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城市，楼房在人们记住名字之前就被替换。

examples.en: The doctor put him on a liquid diet for two days after the operation.
examples.cn: 手术后医生让他吃了两天流食。

examples.en: Investors moved into liquid assets as the outlook darkened.
examples.cn: 前景转暗时，投资者转向流动资产。

examples.en: The market is liquid enough for a large order to be filled in minutes.
examples.cn: 这个市场的流动性足以让大额订单在几分钟内成交。

dict_mnemonic.text: 这个词听起来像「流克的」——能流的、清亮的；钱能立刻流成现金，就是易变现的

root: 拉丁 liquidus「流动的、清澈的」来自 liquere「呈液态」，更深来源不确定；英语 14 世纪吸收为形容词与名词，17 世纪进入语音学，19 世纪进入金融。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow flow: a substance that flows, light that passes through it, motion that runs smoothly, an asset that becomes cash, a market that absorbs orders, funds kept in cash, a consonant that glides, a diet taken as fluid, and a society that will not hold its shape.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿「流动」展开：会流的物质、透过它的光、平滑的运行、变成现金的资产、能吸收订单的市场、以现金持有的资金、滑入邻音的音、以流质进食的饮食，以及无法保持形状的社会。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water sliding down a glass, clear enough to show the coin beneath.
core.cn: 核心意象：水沿玻璃杯滑下，清澈得能看见杯底的硬币。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE AND ITS CLARITY: what flows also lets light through, and both belong to water.
branches.cn: 物质与清澈：会流之物也让光透过，二者都属于水。

branches.en: SMOOTH PASSAGE: motion and consonants alike glide into what follows without a stop.
branches.cn: 平滑过渡：动作与辅音都不阻塞地滑入后接之物。

branches.en: MONEY THAT FLOWS: an asset becomes cash, and the firm keeps its wealth in that form.
branches.cn: 会流的钱：资产变成现金，企业以该形式持有财富。

branches.en: THE MARKET'S DEPTH: many ready buyers let a large order pass without moving the price.
branches.cn: 市场的深度：众多现成买家让大额订单通过而不推动价格。

branches.en: CARE AND METAPHOR: a diet taken as fluid, and a society whose arrangements will not hold their shape.
branches.cn: 照护与隐喻：以流质进食的饮食，以及安排无法定形的社会。

intro.en: Liquid is a Latin adjective for flowing or clear; the same root supplies the noun for liquidity, the verb for melting and the drink called liquor.
intro.cn: liquid 是表示「流动、清澈」的拉丁形容词；同一词根给出表示流动性的名词、表示熔化的动词，以及名为 liquor 的酒。

latinIntro.en: Latin liquere and liquidus stand behind this whole family, from liquid and liquidity to liquefy and liquor.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 liquere 与 liquidus 支撑整个词族，从 liquid、liquidity 到 liquefy 与 liquor。

intro.cn: strategic 来自希腊语中表示将军的词。

items.en: Strategia meant the art of a general.
items.cn: strategia 意为将军的技艺。

items.en: Strategique named the art of planning.

items.en: Strategic entered English for military plans.
items.cn: strategic 以军事谋划之义进入英语。

items.en: Strategic broadened to business and choices.

note.en: Strategic is compared with look-alike words and with words for planned action.

definition_zh: 很少；不常；难得；罕见地
definition_en: not often; hardly ever; in an uncommon manner
core_image: 日历上大片空白的格子，只偶尔落下一笔
scene: 日历翻过一页又一页，大多数格子都是空白的。 She rarely speaks in front of a crowd.
sceneCN: 这里 rarely 是「很少」（第 1 个义项：不常发生）；句意为她很少在众人面前讲话。画面里可留意：大片空白的日历格、偶尔的一点墨迹。

derivatives.zh: rarely 去掉 -ly，指稀有的、罕见的
rare 加 -ity，指罕见、珍品
rare 加 -fy 与 -ed，指变得稀薄的

senses.title: Not often
senses.definition: not often, of an action or event
senses.definitionCN: 动作或事件不常发生
senses.example: She rarely speaks in front of a crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她很少在众人面前讲话。
senses.why: Rarely is rare with the adverb ending, so it says that something happens in a scarce, uncommon way.
senses.whyCN: rarely 是 rare 加副词词尾，说明某事以稀少、不常见的方式发生。

senses.title: Hardly ever
senses.definition: almost never, a stronger degree of the same idea
senses.definitionCN: 几乎从不，是同一意思的更强程度
senses.example: Such storms rarely reach this coast.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的风暴难得抵达这片海岸。
senses.why: When the adverb is stressed or paired with if ever, it moves from seldom to almost never.
senses.whyCN: 当这个副词被重读或与 if ever 连用时，它就从「很少」推向「几乎从不」。

senses.title: In an uncommon way
senses.definition: in a manner that is uncommon, used in formal or literary style
senses.definitionCN: 以一种不常见的方式，用于正式或书面语体
senses.example: The word is rarely used in speech.
senses.exampleCN: 这个词在口语中罕见地使用。
senses.why: The bare sense of rare is uncommon, and the adverb can still point at the manner itself rather than at frequency.
senses.whyCN: rare 的本义就是不常见，副词仍可指向方式本身，而不只是频率。

intro.en: Rarely is rare with the English adverb ending -ly, and rare goes back to Latin rarus, thinly spread.
intro.cn: rarely 是 rare 加上英语副词词尾 -ly，而 rare 可追溯到拉丁语 rarus（分布稀疏）。

items.en: Rarus meant thinly spread or uncommon, the root shared with rare.
items.cn: rarus 意为分布稀疏或不常见，是与 rare 共有的词根。

items.en: English formed the adjective rare from the Latin word, meaning seldom found.
items.cn: 英语从拉丁词构成形容词 rare，意为难得一见。

items.en: The ending -ly turned rare into an adverb meaning in a rare manner, hence not often.
items.cn: 词尾 -ly 把 rare 变成副词，意为以稀少的方式，因此就是「不常」。

items.en: Middle English used rarely for what happens seldom, and the word settled into everyday speech.
items.cn: 中古英语用 rarely 指很少发生的事，这个词逐渐进入日常语言。

items.en: Modern English uses rarely as the plain adverb of not often, and in formal style for in an uncommon way.
items.cn: 现代英语用 rarely 作「不常」的普通副词，并在正式文体中表示「以不常见的方式」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the base word and its relatives; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of low frequency.
note.cn: 形近组收本词原形与近亲；近义组收表示低频的副词。

normalIntro.en: The adverb works on the adjective rare and turns scarcity into frequency: what is done in a rare way is done seldom.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词把形容词 rare 的稀少变成频率：以稀少方式做的事，就是很少做。

normal.en: Rarely is rare with -ly: what happens in a rare way happens seldom.
normal.cn: rarely 是 rare 加 -ly：以稀少方式发生的事就是很少发生。

normal.en: Rarely and seldom mean the same, but rarely is the more common adverb in writing.
normal.cn: rarely 与 seldom 同义，但 rarely 在书面语中更常用。

normal.en: Rarely is stronger when it means hardly ever, close to never.
normal.cn: 当 rarely 意为 hardly ever 时更强，接近 never。

normal.en: She rarely speaks means the speaking is the exception, not the rule.
normal.cn: She rarely speaks 意为开口是例外，不是常态。

normal.en: The word keeps the Latin picture of something thinly spread across time.
normal.cn: 这个词保留了拉丁语「某物在时间中分布稀疏」的画面。

abstract.en: Rarely marks the gaps in a pattern, not the pattern itself.
abstract.cn: rarely 标记的是图案中的空隙，而不是图案本身。

abstract.en: What happens rarely is noticed precisely because it is not routine.
abstract.cn: 很少发生的事之所以被注意到，正因为它不是常规。

abstract.en: To say rarely is to measure absence more than presence.
abstract.cn: 说 rarely，衡量的缺席多于在场。

examples.en: She rarely speaks in front of a crowd.
examples.cn: 她很少在众人面前讲话。

examples.en: He rarely, if ever, loses his temper.

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「空白的日历」——一格又一格都没写字，rarely 就是很少、不常。

root: 拉丁语 rarus（稀疏、罕见）→ 英语 rare + 副词后缀 -ly → rarely；同族有 rare、rarity、rarefied。

sensesIntro.en: The core is low frequency; the senses divide into plain not-often, almost-never, and the formal sense of doing something in an uncommon way.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是低频；义项分为普通的「不常」、更强的「几乎从不」，以及正式的「以不常见方式」。

branches.en: blank squares on a calendar
branches.cn: 日历上大片空白的格子

branches.en: a door that almost never opens
branches.cn: 几乎从不打开的门

branches.en: a word used only in formal writing
branches.cn: 只在正式文字中使用的词

branches.en: seldom and almost never
branches.cn: 很少与几乎从不

branches.en: an act almost never done, done in an odd way
branches.cn: 几乎不做的事，以古怪方式做

intro.en: The word is a Latin root with two English layers, the adjective rare and the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁词根加两层英语成分：形容词 rare 与副词词尾 -ly。

latinIntro.en: Latin rarus, thinly spread, is the recorded source of the root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rarus（分布稀疏）是这个词根有记录可考的来源。

definition_zh: 组成部分；部件；成分；要素；组成的
definition_en: one of the parts that together make a whole machine, system or idea
core_image: 一台拆开的收音机，桌上散着一颗颗零件
scene: 修车师傅把拆下的零件按顺序摆在布上。 Each component must go back in its exact place.
sceneCN: 这里 component 指「组成部分」（第 1 个义项：构成整体的部件）；句意是每个零件都必须装回它原来的确切位置。

derivatives.zh: 成分的；要素的
零部件总称
组成；构成
构成；作品

senses.title: A part of a machine
senses.definition: one of several parts that make up a machine or device
senses.definitionCN: 组成机器或装置的若干部分之一
senses.example: The factory makes engine components.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂生产发动机部件。
senses.why: A machine can be taken apart into pieces, and each piece keeps a clear job.
senses.whyCN: 机器可以拆成零件，而每个零件都有明确的职责。

senses.title: An element of a whole
senses.definition: one part of a larger system, plan or idea
senses.definitionCN: 更大系统、计划或想法中的一部分
senses.example: Trust is a key component of teamwork.
senses.exampleCN: 信任是团队合作的关键要素。
senses.why: Not every part is metal; a system can be held together by an idea.
senses.whyCN: 并非每个部分都是金属做的；一个系统也能靠理念维系。

senses.title: Serving as one part
senses.definition: used to describe a part that helps to form a whole
senses.definitionCN: 用来描述有助于构成整体的部分
senses.example: The component parts are listed on the box.
senses.exampleCN: 各个组成部件都列在盒子上。
senses.why: The adjective simply turns the noun into a label for the part itself.
senses.whyCN: 形容词用法只是把这个名词变成对部件本身的标注。

intro.en: Component comes from Latin componere, to put together, and names a part that has been placed into a whole.
intro.cn: component 来自拉丁语 componere，意为放在一起，指被放进整体里的一个部分。

items.en: Componere joined com-, together, with ponere, to put.
items.cn: componere 由 com-（一起）与 ponere（放置）组合而成。

items.en: A componens was a part that entered a larger whole.
items.cn: componens 指进入更大整体的一个部分。

items.en: French composant named an element that enters a mixture.
items.cn: 法语 composant 指进入混合物的一个成分。

items.en: English component first described one part of a machine.
items.cn: 英语 component 最初指机器的一个部件。

items.en: It now covers parts of machines, systems and ideas alike.
items.cn: 如今它同样覆盖机器、系统与想法的组成部分。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the ending of component, and the meaning group names other words for a part of a whole.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 component 词尾相近的词，近义组列出其他表示整体的部分的词。

entries.definition: a person who competes against you
a person who argues in favour of something
a thing made of two or more parts
a piece of a whole
one basic part of something larger
a single thing that forms part of a whole

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a machine laid out on a table, then move to systems and to the adjective label.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从摊在桌上的机器开始，再走到系统与形容词用法。

normal.en: Com- is together and pon- is put, so a component is something put in with the rest.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pon- 是放置，component 就是和其他部分放在一起的东西。

normal.en: Take the radio apart and every component still looks useful.
normal.cn: 把收音机拆开，每个零件看起来仍然有用。

normal.en: A team has components too, and trust is one of them.
normal.cn: 团队也有组成部分，信任就是其中之一。

normal.en: Component parts is the phrase you see on the side of a box.
normal.cn: 盒子上写的那句话就是 component parts。

normal.en: One component can break the whole machine if it fails.
normal.cn: 一个部件出问题，就可能让整台机器停摆。

abstract.en: Picture a clock face opened to show its tiny wheels.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钟被打开，露出里面细小的齿轮。

abstract.en: Picture a recipe where each ingredient does one job.
abstract.cn: 想象一份食谱，每种材料各司其职。

abstract.en: Picture one brick missing from a long wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一面长墙上缺了一块砖。

examples.en: Each component was tested before assembly.
examples.cn: 每个部件在装配前都经过测试。

examples.en: Cost is only one component of the decision.
examples.cn: 成本只是这个决定的一个组成部分。

examples.en: The component parts arrived in separate boxes.
examples.cn: 各个组成部件分装在几个盒子里运到。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 component 记成 com（一起）加 pon（放）加 ent：被一起放进整体里的那一块，就是部件。

root: 源自拉丁语 componere（com 一起 + ponere 放置），本义是被放入整体的部分，后指部件、成分与要素。

sensesIntro.en: From a metal part in a machine, to an element of a plan, and finally to the adjective that labels the part.
sensesIntro.cn: 从机器里的金属件，到计划中的要素，最后到标注部件的形容词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a radio taken apart on a table, every part in its own place.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台收音机被拆在桌上，每个零件各占一处。

branches.en: The machine sense is the most physical and the easiest to picture.
branches.cn: 机器义项最具体，也最容易想象。

branches.en: A plan or a team can also be built from parts.
branches.cn: 计划和团队同样可以由部分组成。

branches.en: The adjective simply labels a part as belonging to a whole.
branches.cn: 形容词用法只是标注某部分属于整体。

branches.en: Hardware and ideas are both assembled from smaller pieces.
branches.cn: 硬件和理念都由更小的部分组装而成。

branches.en: Component parts is the same idea used as a description.
branches.cn: component parts 只是把同一个意思用作描述。

intro.en: Component is built on Latin com-, together, plus ponere, to put, with the ending -ent.
intro.cn: component 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、ponere（放置）与词尾 -ent 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base pon- also gives compose, position and deposit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 pon- 还给出 compose、position 与 deposit 这些词。

definition_zh: 道歉；认错；赔不是；公开致歉
definition_en: to say that one is sorry for something one has done; in older use, to speak in defense of a position
core_image: 先摆出自己的说法，最后低下头认错
scene: 深夜的厨房里，男孩把打碎的盘子扫进簸箕，走到母亲面前。 He apologized for breaking the plate before she could say a word.
sceneCN: 这里 apologized 是「道歉」（第 1 个义项：为自己做错的事表示歉意）；句意为「在母亲开口之前，他就为打碎盘子道了歉」。画面里有深夜的厨房、扫进簸箕的碎盘子和站在母亲面前的男孩。

pos.zh: 动词：道歉；认错；赔不是；公开致歉
动词（旧式）：为……辩解；替……说话

derivatives.zh: 由希腊语 apologia 经拉丁语借入，义为「道歉；辩解」
由 apology 加形容词后缀 -etic 构成，义为「表示歉意的」
由 apologetic 加副词后缀 -ally 构成，义为「带着歉意地」
由 apology 加 -ist 构成，义为「辩护者」，保留较古的「辩解」义

senses.title: To say one is sorry
senses.definition: to tell someone that one is sorry for a fault, mistake, or harm one has caused
senses.definitionCN: 告诉某人自己为造成的过失、错误或伤害感到抱歉
senses.example: He apologized for breaking the plate before she could say a word.
senses.exampleCN: 在母亲开口之前，他就为打碎盘子道了歉。
senses.why: The Greek source meant a speech of defense; the modern verb keeps the speech but drops the defense, leaving only the admission of fault.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语来源指一篇辩护的言辞；现代动词保留了「言辞」，却去掉了「辩护」，只剩下对过失的承认。

senses.title: To make amends in words
senses.definition: to offer words of regret as a way of repairing a broken relationship
senses.definitionCN: 用表示懊悔的话来修补一段受损的关系
senses.example: You should apologize to her at once.
senses.exampleCN: 你应该马上向她赔个不是。
senses.why: An apology is a small ritual of repair: words stand in for the damage that cannot simply be undone.
senses.whyCN: 道歉是一种小小的修补仪式：用言语代替那些无法直接撤销的损害。

senses.title: To apologize publicly
senses.definition: to state regret openly, often in public or on behalf of an organization
senses.definitionCN: 公开表达歉意，常指在公众场合或代表某个机构致歉
senses.example: The company apologized publicly for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 公司为这次延误公开道了歉。
senses.why: When the fault is public, the repair must also be public; the same speech is now performed before witnesses.
senses.whyCN: 当过失是公开的，修补也必须公开；同一番言辞如今要在众人面前说出。

senses.title: To speak in defense, old use
senses.definition: in older and formal use, to argue in defense of a belief, person, or institution
senses.definitionCN: 在较旧与正式的用法中，为某种信念、人物或机构辩护
senses.example: The old essay apologizes for the customs of its age.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇旧文为它那个时代的习俗作辩护。
senses.why: This is the original Greek sense surviving in formal prose, where the speech is still a shield rather than a confession.
senses.whyCN: 这是希腊语本义在正式散文中的残留，那里的言辞仍是一面盾牌，而不是一份认错书。

intro.en: Apologize descends from a Greek word for a speech of defense, so its oldest meaning is the opposite of the modern confession.
intro.cn: apologize 源自希腊语中表示「辩护之辞」的词，因此它最古老的含义与现代的认错恰好相反。

items.en: Apologia was a speech made in defense, built from apo- 'away from' and logos 'word, speech, account'.
items.cn: apologia 是为辩护而作的言辞，由 apo-「离开」与 logos「言词、说法」构成。

items.en: Latin borrowed the word as apologia, keeping the sense of a formal defense or justification.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 apologia，保留「正式辩护或申辩」的义项。

items.en: English takes apology in the learned sense of a defense, and the word belongs to theology and rhetoric.
items.cn: 英语借入 apology 时取的是学术意义上的「辩护」，这个词属于神学与修辞学。

items.en: The verb apologize appears with the modern sense 'to say one is sorry', while the noun keeps both defense and regret.
items.cn: 动词 apologize 出现，取现代义「表示抱歉」，而名词则同时保留辩护与歉意两种含义。

items.en: The confessional sense dominates everyday use, and the defensive sense retreats into apologist and formal prose.
items.cn: 认错义在日常使用中占主导，辩护义退入 apologist 一词与正式散文里。

items.en: The everyday verb means simply 'say sorry'; its Greek skeleton is visible mainly in the derived nouns.
items.cn: 日常动词的意思就是「说抱歉」；它的希腊骨架主要还能在派生名词里看见。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of admitting fault or making amends.
note.cn: 形近组收由它派生的一族词；近义组收承认过失或作出弥补的动词。

definition_zh: 强调；重点；重音；突出
definition_en: special importance given to something; stress on a word or syllable; force of expression

scene: 老师把关键词写在黑板正中央，又用红笔圈了一遍。 The teacher placed emphasis on the main verb.

senses.title: Special importance
senses.definition: special importance or attention given to something

definition_zh: 细节；详情；详细说明
definition_en: a small fact or feature that is part of a whole
core_image: 一张放大的照片，角落里藏着几样原来看不见的小东西
scene: 修表师傅把放大镜扣在眼上，连齿轮上的一道细痕都要看清。 Every detail of the old watch had to be checked.
sceneCN: 这里 detail 指「细节」（第 1 个义项：构成整体的细小部分）；句意是这块旧表的每个细节都得检查。

derivatives.zh: 详细的
细节处理者
细部处理

senses.title: One small piece of a whole
senses.definition: a single small fact or feature that forms part of something larger
senses.definitionCN: 构成较大整体的一处细小事实或特征
senses.example: Every detail of the old watch had to be checked.
senses.exampleCN: 这块旧表的每个细节都得检查。
senses.why: The whole is not remembered by the eye; the small things are.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛记住的不是整体，而是那些小东西。

senses.title: The full facts
senses.definition: all the particular facts about an event or arrangement
senses.definitionCN: 关于某事件或安排的各项具体事实
senses.example: She explained the details of the contract to us.
senses.exampleCN: 她向我们解释了合同的详情。
senses.why: Small pieces gathered together become the information you need.
senses.whyCN: 小块拼在一起，就成了你真正需要的信息。

senses.title: Set it out point by point
senses.definition: to give all the particular facts about something in writing or speech
senses.definitionCN: 用书面或口头方式把某事的各项事实逐条给出
senses.example: The letter details every step of the journey.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信详述了旅程的每一步。
senses.why: The noun's small pieces become a verb when someone hands them out one by one.
senses.whyCN: 当人把小块一件件递出去，名词就变成了动词。

intro.en: Detail comes from French detail, built on de- and tailler, to cut, so a detail is a small piece cut off from a larger whole.
intro.cn: detail 来自法语 detail，由 de- 与 tailler（切割）构成，所以细节就是从整体上切下来的一小块。

items.en: Tailler meant to cut, and detail named a small cut-off piece.
items.cn: tailler 指切割，detail 指切下来的一小块。

items.en: Painters used it for the small parts of a picture.
items.cn: 画家用它来指一幅画里的小部分。

items.en: English borrowed it for small parts of accounts and designs.
items.cn: 英语借它来指账目与设计中的细小部分。

items.en: Military writers used the verb for listing duties one by one.
items.cn: 军事作者用它的动词形式逐条列出任务。

items.en: In detail is now the standard phrase for a close look.
items.cn: in detail 如今成了表示仔细查看的固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the tail or detail shape, and the meaning group all name one piece of a larger thing.
note.cn: 形近组共用 tail 或 detail 的形状，近义组则都指较大事物中的某一块。

entries.definition: giving many small facts
selling goods to ordinary buyers
a person who makes clothes to fit
one noticeable part of something
a single fact or item
entries.definitionCN: 单独的一条事实或项目

entries.definition: one part of a whole

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a magnifying glass over a watch and end with a letter that lists every step.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从扣在表上的放大镜开始，落到一封列出每一步的信。

normal.en: A detail is a small piece cut off so it can be studied alone.
normal.cn: 细节是被切下来、好单独研究的一小块。

normal.en: De- plus tailler is cutting: the whole is sliced thin.
normal.cn: de- 加 tailler 就是切：把整体切成薄片。

normal.en: The devil is in the detail because the small piece decides.
normal.cn: 关键藏在细节里，因为决定成败的正是那一小块。

normal.en: In detail means you have stopped stepping back.
normal.cn: in detail 就是不再往后退着看。

normal.en: A detailed plan is a plan that has been cut into small pieces.
normal.cn: 详细的计划，就是被切成许多小块的计划。

abstract.en: Picture a lens bringing one scratch into focus.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚镜片把一道划痕放到清晰处。

abstract.en: Picture a page of a contract with one clause circled.
abstract.cn: 想象合同的一页，其中一条被圈了起来。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny screw lying beside a whole watch.
abstract.cn: 想象整只表旁边躺着一颗小螺丝。

examples.en: Every detail of the old watch had to be checked.
examples.cn: 这块旧表的每个细节都得检查。

examples.en: She explained the details of the contract to us.
examples.cn: 她向我们解释了合同的详情。

examples.en: The letter details every step of the journey.
examples.cn: 这封信详述了旅程的每一步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 detail 记成「地忒细」：de 向下看，tail 像「细尾」，越往下看越细，就是细节。

root: 来自法语 detail，由 de- 与 tailler（切割）构成。本义是从整体上切下来的一小块，画家用它指画中的小部分，后来泛指一切构成整体的细小事实，又作动词表示逐条说明。

sensesIntro.en: From a small piece cut from the whole, to the set of all such pieces, to the act of handing them out one by one.
sensesIntro.cn: 从整体上切下的一小块，到所有小块的总和，再到把它们一件件递出去的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small piece cut from a larger surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：从较大表面上切下来的一小块。

branches.en: The first sense is one piece examined under the lens.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是镜片下被察看的那一小块。

branches.en: The second sense is the pile of such pieces gathered up.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是这样的小块被聚成的一堆。

branches.en: The third sense is the act of setting them out in order.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是把它们按顺序摆出来的动作。

branches.en: One piece and the full set differ only in number.
branches.cn: 一小块与完整的一套，差别只在数量。

branches.en: Facts gathered can be handed on to someone else.
branches.cn: 收集起来的事实，可以再交给别人。

intro.en: Detail grows words for the cutting of small pieces, including the shop that sells in small pieces.
intro.cn: detail 长出与切小片有关的一族词，也包括把货物零散卖出的店铺。

latinIntro.en: The base is French tailler, to cut, from Latin talea, a cutting or a stick.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词基是法语 tailler（切割），源于拉丁语 talea（切下的枝条）。

definition_zh: 男孩；少年；小伙子；（英，非正式）哥们儿；马夫；农场小伙计
definition_en: a boy or young man, and in British informal use a male friend or workmate; also a dated word for a stable boy
core_image: 街角一个背着书包、吹着口哨跑过的少年
scene: 傍晚的街角，几个刚下班的年轻人靠在栏杆上聊天。 A young lad in a paint-stained jacket told the others how his first day at work had gone.
sceneCN: 这里 lad 指「小伙子、年轻男孩」（第 1 个义项）；句意为一个外套沾着油漆的小伙子在讲他第一天上班的经历。图中可辨识物件：街角护栏、沾漆的外套、旧背包。

pos.zh: 男孩；少年；小伙子；哥们儿

derivatives.zh: 由 lad 加指小后缀 -ie 构成，多用于苏格兰英语，义为「小伙子；小家伙」
由 lad 加 -ish 构成，形容粗放、爱闹的年轻男性做派
由 lad 加女性后缀 -ette 构成，指举止像小伙子的年轻女性

senses.title: A boy or young man
senses.definition: a boy or young man, often one who is lively or comes from an ordinary working background
senses.definitionCN: 男孩或年轻男子，常指活泼或出身普通劳动阶层的年轻人
senses.example: A young lad was kicking a ball against the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小伙子正对着墙踢球。
senses.why: Lad first named a male servant of low rank, so the word kept a plain, unpretentious tone when it widened to mean any boy or young man.
senses.whyCN: lad 最初指地位低下的男仆，因此当它扩大为泛指男孩、年轻人时，保留了朴素、不端架子的语气。

senses.title: A male friend or workmate
senses.definition: used in British informal speech for a man among friends, especially a workmate or teammate
senses.definitionCN: 英式口语中用来称呼朋友圈或工友、队友中的男性
senses.example: He went out for a drink with the lads from the warehouse.
senses.exampleCN: 他和仓库的哥们儿出去喝酒了。
senses.why: In a close group, a plain word for a male person turns into a badge of belonging: the lads are the men you work and drink with.
senses.whyCN: 在关系紧密的圈子里，一个指男性的朴素词会变成归属的标记：the lads 就是你一起干活、一起喝酒的那群人。

senses.title: A stable or farm boy
senses.definition: a boy or man who looks after horses or does farm work
senses.definitionCN: 照看马匹或干农活的男孩、男子
senses.example: The lad brushed down the horses before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 天还没亮，马夫就把马刷干净了。
senses.why: Before machines, farms and stables depended on young male helpers, so lad named the age and the job in one word.
senses.whyCN: 在机器出现之前，农场和马厩靠年轻的男性帮手，于是 lad 一个词同时指年龄和这份差事。

intro.en: Lad appears in Middle English as a word for a servant or a young man, and its further origin is not reliably known.
intro.cn: lad 在中古英语中出现，指仆役或年轻男子，更早的来源没有可靠结论。

items.en: The earliest records of lad, from about the thirteenth century, use it for a male servant or a man of low rank.
items.cn: lad 最早的记录大约出现在十三世纪，用来指男仆或地位低下的男子。

items.en: No reliable source has been established; ideas linking it to other languages remain guesses, and an unrecorded northern dialect form is only a suggestion.
items.cn: 它的来源至今没有可靠结论；把它与其他语言相联的想法都仍是猜测，所谓未被记录的北方方言形式也只是推测。

items.en: By the fourteenth century lad also meant simply a boy or a young man, and this everyday sense pushed the servant meaning into the background.
items.cn: 到十四世纪，lad 也已直接指男孩或年轻人，这个日常义项把「仆役」义推到幕后。

items.en: The word settled into ordinary speech and appeared in ballads and plays as a friendly or slightly rough way to name a young man.
items.cn: 这个词进入日常口语，在歌谣和戏剧里成为既亲切又略带粗气的「年轻人」称呼。

items.en: Modern British English keeps lad for a boy and for a mate, while laddie survives mainly in Scotland and laddish describes a style of male behaviour.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留 lad 指男孩和伙伴；laddie 主要活在苏格兰，laddish 则形容一种男性做派。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on lad with familiar suffixes; the near-meaning group gathers other words for a young man or a male friend.
note.cn: 形近组收由 lad 加亲切后缀构成的词；近义组收其他表示年轻男子或男性伙伴的词。

entries.definition: A Scottish and affectionate word for a young lad.
entries.definitionCN: 苏格兰用语，亲切地指小伙子。

entries.definition: Behaving in the noisy, beer-and-football style associated with young men.
entries.definitionCN: 带有年轻人爱闹、喝酒看球那种做派的。

entries.definition: A young woman whose behaviour is modelled on laddish young men.
entries.definitionCN: 举止模仿粗放年轻男性的年轻女性。

entries.definition: A male child or a young male person.
A young man, used especially in writing or older speech.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻人，多用于书面语或较早的说法。

entries.definition: A man, often used in a friendly or slightly old-fashioned way.
entries.definitionCN: 男人，常带亲切或略旧式的口吻。

entries.definition: A friend, especially a workmate or teammate.

normalIntro.en: The word began as a plain name for a low-ranking male servant and grew outward into boy, workmate and friend.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词最初是对低微男仆的朴素称呼，后来向外扩展到男孩、工友和朋友。

normal.en: Lad once meant a male servant, which is why it never sounds grand or formal.
normal.cn: lad 曾指男仆，所以它听起来从来不高贵、不正式。

normal.en: A young lad keeps the plainness and adds youth, the most common modern sense.
normal.cn: a young lad 保留那份朴素又加上年轻，是今天最常见的用法。

normal.en: The lads means the group you belong to, so the word turns friendship into a label.
normal.cn: the lads 指你所属的那群男性，于是这个词把友情变成了标签。

normal.en: Laddie adds a Scots diminutive -ie, making the same word warmer and smaller.
normal.cn: laddie 加上苏格兰指小后缀 -ie，让同一个词更亲昵、更小。

normal.en: Laddish and ladette build on lad to describe a style of behaviour, not a person's age.
normal.cn: laddish 与 ladette 都在 lad 上构词，描述一种行为风格，而不是年龄。

abstract.en: A word can start at the bottom of a household and end up as a friendly shout across a street.
abstract.cn: 一个词可以从家庭最底层的位置出发，最后变成街对面一声亲切的招呼。

abstract.en: The same syllable names a boy, a worker and a friend, because all three are the same person seen from different distances.
abstract.cn: 同一个音节指男孩、工人和朋友，因为三者只是从不同距离看同一个人。

abstract.en: Lad is a reminder that English often keeps its warmest words for the plainest people.
abstract.cn: lad 提醒人：英语常把最温暖的词留给最普通的人。

examples.en: The lad brushed down the horses before dawn.
examples.cn: 天还没亮，马夫就把马刷干净了。

root: 来源不确定；一般认为出现于十三世纪的中古英语，最初指男仆或地位低下的男子，后泛指男孩与年轻人。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a young male of plain background; the word then splits into the working boy, the friend in a group, and the boy who tends horses.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是出身普通的年轻男性；词义随后分出干活的男孩、圈子里的伙伴，以及照看马匹的小伙计。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lanky boy in a worn jacket running past a street corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个穿着旧外套、瘦高的男孩从街角跑过。

branches.cn: 一个男孩对着砖墙踢球

definition_en: a person or thing that uses something, especially a person who uses a service or product
core_image: 一个人低头在手机上一步步按着界面操作
scene: 图书馆新装的借书机前，年轻人排队试着操作，工作人员在一旁教第一次来的读者。 Every new user needs a minute to learn the screen.
sceneCN: 这里 user 是「使用者、用户」（第 1 个义项：使用某物或某项服务的人）；句意为每个新用户都需要一点时间熟悉这块屏幕。低头操作界面的画面，正是这个词的核心。

senses.title: A person who uses a product or service
senses.definition: someone who uses a product, service, or system, especially regularly
senses.definitionCN: 使用某产品、服务或系统的人，尤指经常使用的人
senses.example: The website asks every user to choose a password.
senses.exampleCN: 网站要求每位用户设置一个密码。
senses.why: The verb names the act of putting something to work; adding the agent suffix marks the person doing it.
senses.whyCN: 动词指「让东西干活」，加上表人的后缀，就指做这件事的那个人。

senses.title: Someone who takes drugs
senses.definition: a person who takes a drug, often habitually
senses.definitionCN: 服用药物的人，常指长期吸食毒品者
senses.example: The clinic helps long-term drug users rebuild their lives.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所帮助长期吸毒的人重建生活。
senses.why: A drug is also something taken into the body, so the same word carries over to the person who takes it.
senses.whyCN: 药物同样是进入身体的东西，于是这个词也延伸到了服用它的人身上。

senses.title: A device or person consuming a resource
senses.definition: a person or organisation that consumes water, power, or another supply
senses.definitionCN: 消耗水、电或其他资源的个人或机构
senses.example: The village is the largest water user in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子是山谷里用水最多的一方。
senses.why: Since use also means spending a supply, an agent noun can describe whoever draws on that supply.
senses.whyCN: 既然 use 还有「耗用」之义，表人的名词自然也能指取用这份资源的那一方。

senses.title: A person skilled in handling something
senses.definition: a person who knows how to handle a tool or a situation well
senses.definitionCN: 懂得把工具或局面用得熟练的人
senses.example: He is a skilful user of words, able to calm any room.
senses.exampleCN: 他很会用词，能让任何场合安静下来。
senses.why: The same agent noun can praise skill, because the one who uses a thing well is the one who masters it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个表人名词也能表示赞赏：把东西用得好的人，就是掌握它的人。

intro.en: The agent suffix -er, native to English, added to the borrowed verb use.
intro.cn: 英语本土的表人后缀 -er 加在借入动词 use 之上。

items.en: The suffix -ere made agent nouns, as in writer and baker, and is still fully productive.
items.cn: 后缀 -ere 构成表人名词，如 writer、baker，至今仍能自由造词。

items.en: The base comes from uti, to use, with its participle usus.
items.cn: 词基来自 uti（使用）及其分词 usus。

items.en: The verb reached English through French as user, to use.
items.cn: 这个动词经法语 user（使用）进入英语。

items.en: User appears early for anyone who uses a thing, with no link to machines.
items.cn: user 早期泛指使用某物的人，与机器无关。

items.en: With computers and the internet the word becomes the standard term for the person at the screen.
items.cn: 随着电脑与互联网的普及，这个词成为指屏幕前那个人的标准说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the use family, and the near-meaning group names people in terms of what they consume or control.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 use 词族，近义组则从消耗或掌控的角度来称呼人。

normalIntro.en: A plain agent noun: the one who uses is the user, exactly as a writer writes.
normalIntro.cn: 一个朴素的表人名词：谁是用的那个人，谁就是 user，正如写的人叫 writer。

normal.en: User follows the writer and baker pattern of verb plus -er.
normal.cn: user 走的是 writer、baker 那样「动词加 -er」的路子。

normal.en: User name and password are fixed pairs in every login box.
normal.cn: user name 与 password 是每个登录框里的固定搭配。

normal.en: Heavy user suggests a habit, while first-time user suggests novelty.
normal.cn: heavy user 暗示习惯，first-time user 暗示初次接触。

normal.en: The adjective is user-friendly, a modern compound.
normal.cn: 形容词形式是 user-friendly，属于现代复合词。

normal.en: Drug user is a medical or social term, not a technical one.
normal.cn: drug user 是医学或社会用语，并非技术术语。

abstract.en: Picture a queue at a self-service machine, each person learning the screen.
abstract.cn: 想象自助机前排着队，每个人都在学怎么用那块屏幕。

abstract.en: Hear the click of a login page opening on a phone.
abstract.cn: 听手机上一声轻响，登录页弹出。

abstract.en: See worn spots on a keyboard where the same fingers always land.
abstract.cn: 看键盘上被同一副手指磨出来的那几处。

examples.en: Each user of the shared bike must lock it afterwards.
examples.cn: 每位共享单车用户都必须之后锁好车。

examples.en: The guide was written for users with no technical training.
examples.cn: 这本指南是写给没有技术背景的使用者的。

examples.en: A heavy user of electricity will notice the bill at once.
examples.cn: 用电大户立刻就能感到账单的变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「优择」——挑来挑去，最后选中使用的就是用户。

root: 本土表人后缀 -er 加动词 use（拉丁语 uti / usus，经古法语 user），义为「使用的人」

sensesIntro.en: One agent noun branches from using products to taking drugs, from drawing on a supply to mastering a skill.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个表人名词，从使用产品分到吸食药物，从耗用资源分到精于此道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person at a screen, learning how it works.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人面对着屏幕，熟悉它的用法。

branches.en: The product branch: the person a service is built for.
branches.cn: 产品分支：服务所围绕的那个人。

branches.en: The drug branch: the body as the thing being used.
branches.cn: 药物分支：身体成了被使用的对象。

branches.en: The resource branch: whoever draws water or power.
branches.cn: 资源分支：取水取电的那一方。

branches.en: The skill branch: skill turns a user into a master.
branches.cn: 技艺分支：熟练使使用者变成行家。

branches.en: The consumption branch: using always takes something up.
branches.cn: 消耗分支：凡是使用总要占用掉一些什么。

intro.en: A verb plus the native agent suffix: the person who performs the action.
intro.cn: 动词加本土表人后缀：执行这个动作的人。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin uti and its participle usus; the suffix -er is Germanic, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 词基是拉丁语 uti 及其分词 usus；-er 后缀是日耳曼语成分，不是拉丁语。

definition_zh: 扔；抛；丢弃；放弃；卡盘；夹头；（口语）轻拍
definition_en: to throw something carelessly, to discard or give up something, or a device that clamps and holds a tool or workpiece in a machine
core_image: 随手一抛：东西没被郑重地放下，而是被轻轻甩了出去
scene: 工间休息时，工人看见口袋里的碎纸团。 He opened his fist and gave the paper a careless chuck into the bin.
sceneCN: 这里 chuck 是名词「随手一抛」（第 4 个义项：不经意的投掷动作）；句意是他张开手掌，把纸团随随便便抛进垃圾桶，突出动作的随意和不郑重。

derivatives.zh: 由 chuck（路面）+ hole（洞）构成，义为「路面坑洼」（美式口语）
由 chuck 加昵称后缀构成，义为「小鸡」（儿语）
由 chuck 与 full 构成的变体，义为「塞得满满的」（美国方言）

senses.title: To throw something carelessly
senses.definition: to throw something in a casual or careless way
senses.definitionCN: 随意地、不太郑重地把某物扔出或抛出
senses.example: She chucked her coat on the bed and flopped down beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 她把外套往床上一扔，一屁股躺倒在旁边。
senses.why: The core image is a light, unceremonious toss: the arm flicks and the object flies, with no care about where it lands.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是轻巧随意的抛掷：手臂一甩东西就飞出去，完全不在乎落在哪里，所以最早的动词义就是「随手扔」。

senses.title: To discard or get rid of something
senses.definition: to throw something away because you do not want it any more
senses.definitionCN: 把不要的东西处理掉、丢弃
senses.example: These old shoes are finished—just chuck them out.
senses.exampleCN: 这双旧鞋没法穿了，直接扔掉吧。
senses.why: If tossing is careless, the natural next step is tossing into the bin: the throw becomes a deliberate act of disposal.
senses.whyCN: 既然「扔」是不经意的，往垃圾桶一扔就成了主动丢弃：投掷动作延伸为「处理掉不要的东西」。

senses.title: To give up a job, plan, or relationship
senses.definition: to give up or abandon something such as a job or a plan, often suddenly
senses.definitionCN: 突然或干脆地放弃工作、计划或关系
senses.example: After one terrible month, he chucked the job and went travelling.
senses.exampleCN: 过了糟糕的一个月，他干脆辞了职去旅行。
senses.why: Discarding a thing extends metaphorically to discarding commitments: you 'throw away' the job or plan as if it were rubbish.
senses.whyCN: 丢掉物品的意象投射到抽象层面：把工作或计划像垃圾一样「一扔了之」，于是引申出放弃、辞掉之义。

senses.title: A casual throw; the act of tossing
senses.definition: an act of throwing something lightly or carelessly
senses.definitionCN: 一次轻率随意的抛掷动作
senses.example: With a quick chuck of the ball, the game started.
senses.exampleCN: 球被随手一抛，比赛就开始了。
senses.why: The action verb is converted into a noun naming the action itself, a very common English pattern.
senses.whyCN: 动词转化为名词指称动作本身，这是英语里极常见的用法，「扔一下」变成「一抛」这个名词。

senses.title: A clamping device in a machine
senses.definition: a device on a lathe or drill that grips the tool or the workpiece tightly
senses.definitionCN: 车床或钻床上夹紧刀具或工件的装置
senses.example: Loosen the chuck before you change the drill bit.
senses.exampleCN: 换钻头之前先松开卡盘。
senses.why: Another chuck word, of different origin, means a grip or clamp; mechanics borrowed it for the device that 'bites' and holds the tool.
senses.whyCN: 机械领域借用了另一个来源的 chuck（咬合、夹持），指那种像嘴巴一样咬紧刀具的夹持装置，与「扔」义只是拼写巧合。

senses.title: A cut of beef from the shoulder
senses.definition: a cut of meat from the lower neck and shoulder of a cow
senses.definitionCN: 牛颈部下方与肩部之间切下的一块肉
senses.example: Chuck makes a rich stew because it has just enough fat.
senses.exampleCN: 牛肩肉脂肪适中，炖出来的汤很浓郁。
senses.why: This sense again comes from a separate chuck word meaning a piece or cut, showing how one spelling gathers several unrelated histories.
senses.whyCN: 这一义来自另一个意为「一块、一份」的 chuck，说明同一个拼写背后聚着几条互不相干的词源线索。

senses.title: To pat or touch someone playfully
senses.definition: to tap someone gently, especially under the chin, as an affectionate gesture
senses.definitionCN: 亲昵地轻拍某人，尤指轻托下巴
senses.example: Grandmother gave the baby a playful chuck under the chin.
senses.exampleCN: 祖母亲昵地轻托了一下宝宝的下巴。
senses.why: A gentle, playful movement sits close to a light throw in feeling, so the same casual word covers this affectionate tap.
senses.whyCN: 轻巧、玩闹的动作与「轻抛」在感觉上很接近，同一个随意的词便也覆盖了这种亲昵的轻拍。

senses.title: To utter a clucking sound; to cluck
senses.definition: to make a short clucking sound, as a hen does, or to call chickens with such a sound
senses.definitionCN: 发出类似母鸡的咯咯短促叫声，或用这种声音唤鸡
senses.example: The old hen chuck-chucked whenever strangers came near.
senses.exampleCN: 只要有生人靠近，老母鸡就咯咯地叫个不停。
senses.why: This is likely an imitative word, echoing the hen's call directly; it is probably yet another separate chuck.
senses.whyCN: 这一义很可能是拟声词，直接模仿母鸡的叫声，多半又是一条独立的 chuck 词源线索。

intro.en: Chuck is a spelling that gathers several distinct histories: a casual-throw verb of uncertain deeper origin, a separate clamp word, a meat-cut term, and an imitation of a hen's call.
intro.cn: chuck 这个拼写背后聚着几条互不相干的历史：一条来源不深的「随手扔」动词线索、一条独立的「夹持」线索、一块肉的名称，以及对母鸡叫声的模仿。

items.en: The verb chukken appears in Middle English meaning to throw carelessly and also to cluck like a hen; its deeper origin is uncertain, and it may be imitative or related to chick.
items.cn: 中古英语出现动词 chukken，既表「随手扔」，也表「咯咯叫」；更深来源不确定，一般认为可能是拟声，或与 chick（小鸡）相关。

items.en: The affectionate use develops: to chuck someone means to pat them gently, and Chuck becomes a familiar nickname for Charles, from terms of endearment for a 'darling'.
items.cn: 亲昵用法发展起来：chuck someone 表示轻轻拍打，Chuck 又成为 Charles 的昵称，源于表示「心肝宝贝」的爱称。

items.en: A separate chuck meaning 'a grip, a bite' appears in dialect; machinists later adopt it for the clamping device, giving the technical sense of drill chuck.
items.cn: 方言中出现另一个意为「咬合、夹持」的 chuck；机械工匠后来用它称呼夹紧装置，于是有了钻夹头这一技术义。

items.en: The noun chuck names a cut of beef from the neck and shoulder, generally thought to come from the same dialect word for a piece or chunk of meat.
items.cn: 名词 chuck 开始指牛颈肩部切下的一块肉，一般认为来自方言中表示「一块肉」的同一个词。

items.en: Phrasal verbs multiply in colloquial speech: chuck up (give up), chuck out (discard, expel), chuck in (add casually), making the verb a workhorse of informal English.
items.cn: 口语中短语动词大量出现：chuck up（放弃）、chuck out（扔掉、赶出）、chuck in（顺手加上），使这个动词成为非正式英语里的多用词。

items.en: Today chuck covers casual throwing, disposal, giving up, the machine clamp, the meat cut, and the chicken's call—several histories hiding under one short spelling.
items.cn: 今天 chuck 同时涵盖随手扔、丢弃、放弃、机械卡盘、牛肩肉和母鸡叫声——一个短短的拼写之下藏着好几条历史线索。

note.en: Chuck hides several word histories under one spelling, so look-alikes come from different roots, and near-meaning words cluster around casual throwing and discarding.
note.cn: chuck 一个拼写下藏着多条词源线索，所以形近词常来自不同词根，而近义词则围绕「随手扔、丢弃」这个义场聚集。

entries.definition: a thick, solid piece cut or broken off something
entries.definitionCN: 厚实的一块、一大块；与 chuck 仅一字母之差，词源相关但义为「块」而非「扔」。

entries.definition: a young bird, especially a young chicken
entries.definitionCN: 雏鸟；小鸡；一般认为与 chuck 的拟声线索有关联，但义为「小鸡」。

entries.definition: a soft white limestone used for writing or drawing
entries.definitionCN: 粉笔；白垩；只是拼写和发音相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: to throw something lightly or casually
entries.definitionCN: 轻抛、随手扔；与 chuck 的随意抛掷义几乎重合，但 toss 也指摇摆、抛硬币。

entries.definition: to throw something with force and lack of care
entries.definitionCN: 用力乱扔、猛抛；力道比 chuck 大，情绪更激烈。

entries.definition: to get rid of something you no longer want
entries.definitionCN: 丢弃、舍弃；正式用语，对应 chuck 的「扔掉」义但语气书面。

normalIntro.en: Build the memory from sound, spelling, phrasal verbs and real usage.
normalIntro.cn: 从发音、拼写、短语动词和真实用法几个角度搭记忆。

normal.en: Chuck sounds like a short, punchy flick of the arm—the sound itself feels like a quick throw.
normal.cn: chuck 发音短促有力，听上去就像手臂一甩的那一下，音与「随手扔」的动作呼应。

normal.en: chuck away = throw away: the phrase rhymes with itself, so remember it as a doubled 'throw'.
normal.cn: chuck away 与 throw away 结构完全平行，把它记成「双份的扔掉」即可。

normal.en: In the workshop, the chuck grips the drill bit—picture a mechanical hand that 'bites' the tool.
normal.cn: 在车间里，卡盘咬住钻头——想象一只机械手把工具紧紧咬住。

normal.en: At the butcher's, ask for chuck beef: the shoulder cut that stews well.
normal.cn: 在肉铺要 chuck beef：炖汤好吃的牛肩肉。

normal.en: Nickname memory: Chuck is the friendly short form of Charles—an informal word for an informal set of meanings.
normal.cn: 昵称记忆：Chuck 是 Charles 的随和简称——一个随意的词配一整套随意义项。

abstract.en: Imagine sweeping a desk with one stroke: papers, plans and worries all get chucked into the bin.
abstract.cn: 想象一把扫过桌面：文件、计划和烦恼统统被抛进垃圾桶。

abstract.en: Picture a machine jaw snapping shut—tight, precise, the exact opposite of a careless throw.
abstract.cn: 想象机械钳口咔哒合拢——紧而精准，恰是「随手一扔」的反面。

abstract.en: Hear the hen's chuck-chuck in the yard: the same short syllable clucking in the morning air.
abstract.cn: 听院子里母鸡咯咯的叫声：同一个短音节在清晨的空气里回响。

examples.en: He chucked the ball to his brother and ran to first base.
examples.cn: 他把球随手抛给弟弟，然后冲向一垒。

examples.en: Tighten the chuck firmly, or the drill bit will slip.
examples.cn: 把卡盘拧紧，否则钻头会打滑。

examples.en: She chucked everything into a suitcase and left for the airport.
examples.cn: 她把所有东西一股脑塞进箱子就动身去机场了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「恰克」——东西恰好卡在钳口里：一读「恰克」，就想到卡盘恰好夹紧的样子；发音短促，又像随手一抛的利落劲儿。

root: 一般认为 chuck（扔）是中古英语 chukken 的延续，深层来源不确定，可能是拟声或与 chick（小鸡）同源；机械义的卡盘与牛肉义的牛肩肉来自另外两条独立的 chuck 线索（方言「咬合、夹持」与「一块肉」），存疑处已在词源部分标注。

sensesIntro.en: From a careless throw, the meanings fan out into disposal, giving up, the noun for the throw itself, and then into the unrelated clamp, meat-cut, pat and cluck senses.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「随手一扔」出发，词义先扩散为丢弃、放弃和指称抛掷动作本身的名词，再接入互不相干的卡盘、牛肩肉、轻拍与咯咯叫诸义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a light, careless flick of the arm—the object flies without ceremony
core.cn: 核心意象：手臂轻巧一甩，东西毫无仪式感地飞了出去

branches.en: casual throwing in everyday speech
branches.cn: 日常口语里的随手扔、轻抛

branches.en: throwing into the bin becomes discarding
branches.cn: 往垃圾桶一扔成为丢弃、处理掉

branches.en: throwing away commitments; naming the throw
branches.cn: 像扔垃圾一样辞掉工作、放弃计划，以及「一抛」这个动作名词

branches.en: the clamp that grips tools in machines
branches.cn: 机床中夹紧刀具的卡盘、夹头

branches.en: beef cut, affectionate pat and the hen's cluck
branches.cn: 牛肩肉、亲昵轻拍与母鸡咯咯叫等旁支义项

intro.en: Chuck is a short native word, so its affix story is mainly about the phrasal verbs and small endings that attach to it.
intro.cn: chuck 是个短小的本族语词，它的构词故事主要体现在短语动词和附加的小后缀上。

latinIntro.en: Chuck has no Latin root; the Latin-linked words below are only the neighbouring machinery terms that appear in the same workshop vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: chuck 没有拉丁词根；下面列出的拉丁系条目只是车间词汇里与它相邻的机械术语，并非同源。

items.example: They chucked him out of the club.
items.exampleCN: 他们把他赶出了俱乐部。

items.example: He chucked up his job last May.

items.meaning: to add casually or give as a bonus
items.example: They chucked in a free bag with the camera.
items.exampleCN: 买相机他们还额外送了一个包。

items.meaningCN: 过去式与过去分词后缀

items.meaning: marks ongoing action or noun use
marks third-person singular verbs or plural nouns
items.meaningCN: 三单动词与名词复数后缀

items.meaning: a chuck that holds a drill bit

items.example: The van was chuck-full of boxes.

latinEntries.meaningCN: 抓住、握住；派生出 pliers（钳）、apprehend 等词，与 chuck 的「夹持」义属同一功能场而非同源

definition_zh: 打赌；赌注；（口语）敢说
definition_en: to risk money on a result, or the money risked

scene: 他攥着票根盯住冲过终点的马。 He bet ten pounds on the black horse.

senses.title: To risk money on a result
senses.definition: to risk money on the result of an event
senses.definitionCN: 拿钱押在某事的结果上
senses.example: He bet ten pounds on the black horse.
senses.exampleCN: 他押了十英镑在那匹黑马上。
senses.why: This is the core sense, tied to racing and cards.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义，与赛马和纸牌紧密相关。

senses.title: The money risked
senses.definition: the money or thing risked in a bet
senses.definitionCN: 下注时押上的钱或物
senses.example: He lost the bet and paid at once.
senses.exampleCN: 他赌输了，当场付了钱。
senses.why: The verb became a noun for the stake itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词转作名词，指押上的赌注。

senses.title: To feel sure
senses.definition: to say that one is sure about something
senses.definitionCN: 表示对某事很有把握
senses.example: I bet she will call tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我敢说她今晚会打电话来。
senses.why: Everyday speech loosened betting into a confident guess.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语把「下注」放宽为有把握的猜测。

definition_zh: 必不可少的；本质的；要素
definition_en: completely necessary, or forming the basic nature of something
core_image: 一座桥最关键的那块基石，抽掉它整座桥就会塌
scene: 水对所有的生物都是必不可少的，没有它谁也活不了。 Water is essential to all living things, and nothing can survive without it.
sceneCN: 这里 essential 是「必不可少的」（第 1 个义项：缺了就完全无法维持）；句意：水对所有的生物都是必不可少的，没有它谁也活不了。

derivatives.zh: 本质上；基本上
本质；精髓
必要性

senses.title: Completely necessary
senses.definition: so important that something cannot work without it
senses.definitionCN: 重要到没有它就无法运作
senses.example: Sleep is essential for good health.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠对健康必不可少。
senses.why: The word comes from essence, so what is essential belongs to the very being of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个词来自 essence，因此 essential 指属于事物存在本身的东西。

senses.title: Forming the basic nature
senses.definition: forming the central nature of something
senses.definitionCN: 构成某事物的核心性质
senses.example: Freedom is an essential feature of democracy.
senses.exampleCN: 自由是民主的本质特征。
senses.why: The basic nature of a thing is what cannot be removed without changing it.
senses.whyCN: 事物的本质就是抽掉后它就不再是它自己的东西。

senses.title: A basic necessary thing
senses.definition: something that is completely necessary
senses.definitionCN: 完全不可缺少的事物
senses.example: The guide covers the essentials of camping.
senses.exampleCN: 这本指南涵盖了露营的基本要点。
senses.why: The adjective turns into a noun for the necessary things themselves.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词转化为名词，指那些必要的事物本身。

intro.en: Essential comes from Late Latin essentialis, from essentia, being or nature.
intro.cn: essential 源自晚期拉丁语 essentialis，来自 essentia（存在、本性）。

items.en: Essentia means being or nature.
items.cn: essentia 意为存在或本性。

items.en: Essentialis means belonging to the essence.
items.cn: essentialis 意为属于本质的。

items.en: Essential means forming the nature of something.
items.cn: essential 意为构成某事物的本性。

items.en: It also means absolutely necessary.
items.cn: 它也意为绝对必要。

items.en: The plural essentials names necessary items.
items.cn: 复数 essentials 指必需物品。

note.en: Essential is close to necessary and vital, and to essence in meaning.
note.cn: essential 与必要的、至关重要的相近，并与 essence 意义相连。

entries.definition: in basic nature
the basic nature
belief in fixed natures
needed for a purpose

normalIntro.en: Essential is about essence: remove it and the thing loses itself.
normalIntro.cn: essential 关乎 essence：抽掉它，事物就不再是自己。

normal.en: Essential to health means health fails without it.
normal.cn: essential to health 意为没有它健康就会垮。

normal.en: An essential part is one you cannot remove.
normal.cn: an essential part 是你不能去掉的部分。

normal.en: Absolutely essential means there is no substitute.
normal.cn: absolutely essential 意为没有替代品。

normal.en: The bare essentials are the smallest necessary set.
normal.cn: the bare essentials 是最低限度的必需品。

normal.en: Compare vital: vital stresses life, essential stresses necessity.
normal.cn: 对比 vital：vital 强调生命，essential 强调必要。

abstract.en: Picture the one stone that holds up an arch.
abstract.cn: 想象支撑整座拱门的那块石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a recipe missing its key ingredient.
abstract.cn: 想象一份缺少关键原料的食谱。

abstract.en: Think of a key that opens the only door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能打开唯一那扇门的钥匙。

examples.en: It is essential to book early.
examples.cn: 尽早预订是必不可少的。

examples.en: Trust is an essential part of friendship.
examples.cn: 信任是友谊的关键部分。

examples.en: Pack only the essentials for the trip.
examples.cn: 旅行只带必需品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「essence（本质）＋ ial」——属于本质的东西，就是必不可少的；这只是构词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 essentia（存在、本性）→ 晚期拉丁语 essentialis → essential，核心义「属于事物本性、缺之不可」。

sensesIntro.en: Essential first means completely necessary, then belonging to the basic nature, and as a noun it names necessary things.
sensesIntro.cn: essential 先指完全必要，再指属于本质，作名词时指必需品。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the keystone whose removal collapses the arch.
core.cn: 核心意象：抽掉就会让拱门倒塌的拱心石。

branches.en: Complete necessity is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 完全必要是日常义项。

branches.en: The basic nature of a thing is its essence.
branches.cn: 事物的基本性质就是它的本质。

branches.en: As a noun it names necessary items.
branches.cn: 作名词时指必需物品。

branches.en: What belongs to the essence is what cannot be removed.
branches.cn: 属于本质的东西就是不能抽掉的东西。

branches.en: The essentials of a subject are its core points.
branches.cn: 一门学科的 essentials 就是其核心要点。

intro.en: Essential adds -ial to essence, from Latin essentia.
intro.cn: essential 在 essence 上加 -ial，源自拉丁语 essentia。

latinIntro.en: Essentia comes from esse, to be, so essence is the very being of a thing.
latinIntro.cn: essentia 来自 esse（存在），因此本质就是事物的存在本身。

items.example: Esse is the verb of being.
items.exampleCN: esse 是表示存在的动词。

items.example: Essential describes what cannot be removed.
items.exampleCN: essential 描述不能去掉的东西。

definition_zh: 不像；与……不同；和……不一样；（作形容词）不同的；不相像的
definition_en: different from, not similar to, or in contrast to someone or something
core_image: 两枚并排放着的贝壳：一枚细长有纹，一枚扁圆光滑，一眼就看得出不是一家
scene: 姐姐安静地读书，弟弟却一整天都在院子里拆东西，母亲常对客人说他们是完全不同的人。 Unlike her brother, she has never broken a single cup.
sceneCN: 这里 unlike 是「与……不同、不像」（第 1 个义项：表示对比）；句意为和弟弟不同，她从未打碎过一只杯子。两枚并排放着却毫不相像的贝壳，就是这个词的样子。

pos.zh: 不典型的；不像平常那样的
不像……那样（非标准，口语偶见）

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ly 构成，义为「不太可能的」
由本词加 -ness 构成，义为「不相似、不同」
本词去掉 un-，义为「像；如同」
与本词同源，义为「相似的」，多作表语

senses.title: Different from
senses.definition: used to say that one person or thing is different from another
senses.definitionCN: 用来表示某个人或物与另一个不同
senses.example: Unlike his father, he has never enjoyed fishing.
senses.exampleCN: 与他父亲不同，他从来不喜欢钓鱼。
senses.why: The prefix denies likeness while still setting the two people side by side, so the comparison stays visible.
senses.whyCN: 这个前缀否认相像，却仍把两个人并排放着，比较因此看得见。

senses.title: Not similar to in kind
senses.titleCN: 不相像的；不类似的（形容词）
senses.definition: not similar in appearance, character, or nature
senses.definitionCN: 在外观、性格或性质上不相像
senses.example: The two sisters are unlike in almost every way.
senses.exampleCN: 这对姐妹几乎在各方面都不相像。
senses.why: As an adjective the same word drops the second person and simply denies sameness in nature.
senses.whyCN: 作形容词时，同一个词不再针对第二个对象，只是单纯否认性质上的相同。

senses.title: Not like the usual
senses.definition: not typical of a person, so that it surprises those who know them
senses.definitionCN: 不像某人平时那样，因而让熟悉的人感到意外
senses.example: It is unlike her to arrive so late.
senses.exampleCN: 迟到这么久不像她的作风。
senses.why: The comparison is now between a person and their own usual self, which is why the word can sound like surprise.
senses.whyCN: 比较发生在一个人与自己平日的模样之间，因此这个词听起来带着惊讶。

senses.title: To point at a contrast
senses.definition: at the start of a clause, drawing a contrast with what follows
senses.definitionCN: 用于从句开头，与后文形成对比
senses.example: Unlike other cities, this one keeps its trams in the centre.
senses.exampleCN: 与别的城市不同，这座城市把有轨电车保留在市中心。
senses.why: At the head of a clause the preposition sets the second half of the sentence against the first.
senses.whyCN: 放在从句开头时，这个介词把句子的后半段与前半段对立起来。

senses.title: Unlike anything else
senses.definition: in the phrase unlike anything, stressing that no comparison is possible
senses.definitionCN: 在 unlike anything 这一说法中，强调无从比较
senses.example: The storm was unlike anything the village had seen.
senses.exampleCN: 这场风暴是村里人从未见过的。
senses.why: When the second term is anything, the comparison is denied altogether: nothing matches.
senses.whyCN: 当比较的另一项是 anything 时，比较被彻底取消：没有任何东西能相配。

intro.en: Unlike is the native negative prefix on an Old English word for what is like or alike.
intro.cn: unlike 是本土否定前缀加一个古英语表示「相似」的词。

items.en: Gelīc meant of the same form or body, from līc, a body; it became the modern like and alike.
items.cn: 古英语 gelīc 意为「形体相同的」，源于 līc（身体）；后演变为 like 与 alike。

items.en: The prefix un- was already used to deny such adjectives, as in ungelīc.
items.cn: 否定前缀 un- 早已用来否定这类形容词，如 ungelīc。

items.en: The word settled as unlike, and was used both as adjective and as preposition.
items.cn: 这个词固定为 unlike，既可作形容词也可作介词。

items.en: Unlike at the head of a clause became the standard way to open a contrast in written English.
items.cn: 在书面英语中，用 unlike 开头引出对比成了标准做法。

items.en: The derived unlikely took over the sense of not probable, leaving unlike to comparison alone.
items.cn: 派生词 unlikely 承担了「不太可能」的意思，unlike 则只保留比较义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words in un- and like-alike forms; the near-meaning group gathers ways to mark contrast.
note.cn: 形近组收 un- 与 like、alike 一族的词；近义组收表示对比的说法。

entries.definition: Not probable; it points to chance rather than similarity.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不太可能的」，指机会而不指相似。

entries.definition: The noun for the state of being different.
Similar to, or in the same way as; the word without un-.
entries.definitionCN: 介词，义为「像」，即去掉 un- 的词。

entries.definition: Similar to each other; usually after the verb be.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「相似的」，多作表语。

entries.definition: To not like something; close in shape but about feeling, not similarity.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「不喜欢」，形近而意义不同。

entries.definition: The plain and safest comparative phrase in formal writing.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「与……不同」，正式写作中最稳妥。

entries.definition: Marks a sharp difference; more formal and heavier than unlike.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「与……形成对比」，较正式。

entries.definition: Used to turn the sentence towards an opposite case.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「相比之下」，用于转向相反的情形。

entries.definition: A conjunction joining two contrasted clauses in one sentence.
entries.definitionCN: 连词，义为「而」，在同一句中连接两个对比分句。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning not alike; formal and used of things, not people's habits.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不相似的」，较正式，多用于物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the plain un- plus like structure and the contrast phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子使用 un 加 like 的朴素结构，以及这个词出现的对比搭配。

normal.en: Un- means not and like means similar: not similar to.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，like 表示「像」：不像。

normal.en: Unlike her brother, she never breaks a cup: the phrase opens a contrast.
normal.cn: unlike her brother 意为与她弟弟不同；这个短语一开头就摆出对比。

normal.en: Unlike means not like, and it is the opposite of like rather than of likely.
normal.cn: unlike 意为「不像」，反义是 like 而不是 likely。

normal.en: Alike takes no un-: the pair is like and unlike, alike and unalike.
normal.cn: alike 不加 un-：配对的是 like 与 unlike、alike 与 unalike。

normal.en: To call a person unlike their usual self is to stress that this is not their habit.
normal.cn: 用 unlike 说某人反常，就是强调这不像他平时的样子。

abstract.en: Picture two shells of the same weight but a different shape: the hand feels at once that they are not of one family.
abstract.cn: 想象两枚重量相同而形状不同的贝壳：手一摸就知道它们不是一家。

abstract.en: Unlike does not deny a relation; it denies sameness while keeping the comparison.
abstract.cn: unlike 不否认关系，它否认相同，同时保留比较。

abstract.en: Every contrast needs two things put side by side, and the word is the space between them.
abstract.cn: 每个对比都需要两样东西并排，这个词就是它们之间的那段距离。

examples.en: Unlike most of his friends, he walks to work every day.
examples.cn: 与他多数朋友不同，他每天走路上班。

examples.en: The twins are unlike in temperament but close in spirit.
examples.cn: 这对双胞胎性情不同，感情却很好。

examples.en: It is unlike him to complain without a reason.
examples.cn: 无缘无故地抱怨不像他的为人。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安的莱克」——安和莱克完全不像：不像、与……不同

root: 由否定前缀 un- 与古英语 gelīc（形体相同的，源于 līc「身体」）构成，古英语已有 ungelīc；中古英语定型为 unlike，作形容词与介词，近代在句首成为引出对比的标准说法。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of unlike all deny sameness while keeping a comparison: two people, two things, one person and their usual self, two places, or one thing and everything else.
sensesIntro.cn: unlike 的五个义项都否认相同却保留比较：两个人、两样东西、一个人与其平时的样子、两个地方，或一样东西与其余一切。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two shells side by side, obviously not of one family.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚并排的贝壳，一眼就看得出不是一家。

branches.en: THE PAIR: one person set against another, as a preposition.
branches.cn: 对照线：一个人与另一个人相对，作介词。

branches.en: THE SHAPE: the adjective says the two are not alike in nature.
branches.cn: 形状线：形容词说两者性质上并不相像。

branches.en: THE HABIT: a person unlike their usual self.
branches.cn: 习惯线：一个人不像平时的自己。

branches.en: THE OPENING: unlike at the head of a clause sets up the contrast.
branches.cn: 开头线：unlike 置于句首，摆出对比。

branches.en: THE UNMATCHED: unlike anything leaves nothing to compare with.
branches.cn: 无偶线：unlike anything 表示无从比较。

intro.en: Unlike is a native prefix on a native adjective, with English suffixes for the rest of the family.
intro.cn: unlike 是本土前缀加本土形容词，家族其余成员由英语后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin here; the roots are Old English, and later Latin-based synonyms are listed only for comparison.

items.exampleCN: like 与 alike 的祖先。

scene: 教练要求队员每天清晨到场训练。 The team showed real commitment during the long season.
sceneCN: 这里 commitment 指「投入；奉献」（第 2 个义项：全心全意的付出）；句意是这支队伍在漫长的赛季里表现出真正的投入。

derivatives.zh: 承诺；投入

senses.title: A promise to do something
senses.definition: a firm promise that you will do something
senses.definitionCN: 坚定地答应去做某事的保证
senses.example: She made a commitment to call her parents weekly.
senses.exampleCN: 她承诺每周给父母打电话。
senses.why: The -ment ending turns the act of committing into the thing promised.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把承诺的动作变成被承诺下来的那件事。

senses.title: Dedication
senses.definition: steady effort and loyalty given to a person, job or cause
senses.definitionCN: 对某人、某项工作或事业持续付出的努力与忠诚
senses.example: The team showed real commitment during the long season.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在漫长的赛季里表现出真正的投入。
senses.why: A promise kept day after day becomes visible dedication.
senses.whyCN: 一天天兑现的承诺，就变成了看得见的投入。

senses.title: A duty you must carry out
senses.definition: an obligation that takes your time and cannot be ignored
senses.definitionCN: 占用你的时间且无法回避的义务
senses.example: He has family commitments this weekend.
senses.exampleCN: 他这周末有家里的事务要处理。
senses.why: Each promise creates a duty, and the word names those duties in the plural.
senses.whyCN: 每个承诺都造出一份义务，这个词用复数来指这些义务。

intro.en: Commitment is commit plus -ment, the ending that turns an action into a thing.
intro.cn: commitment 由 commit 加 -ment 构成，词尾把动作变成事物。

items.en: Committere meant to entrust or hand over.
items.cn: committere 意为托付或交出。

items.en: Old French commettre supplied the verb commit.
items.cn: 古法语 commettre 提供了动词 commit。

items.en: English commit covered entrusting and carrying out acts.
items.cn: 英语 commit 兼指托付与实施行为。

items.en: Commitment appeared as the state of being pledged.
items.cn: commitment 出现，表示已被许诺约束的状态。

items.en: It widened to mean loyalty to work, people and causes.
items.cn: 它的含义扩展到对工作、他人与事业的忠诚。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns built on the commit stem, while the meaning group names promises and duties.
note.cn: 形近组收的是建立在 commit 词干上的名词，近义组列出承诺与义务。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a spoken promise, then move to daily dedication and to the duties that pile up around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一句说出口的承诺开始，再走到日复一日的投入与由此堆积的事务。

normal.en: Commit is the act, commitment is the thing you are now held to.
normal.cn: commit 是动作，commitment 是你此后必须遵守的那件事。

normal.en: A commitment kept for years looks exactly like dedication.
normal.cn: 坚持多年的承诺，看起来就是投入。

normal.en: Make a commitment, then honour it: two verbs, one promise.
normal.cn: 作出承诺，然后履行承诺：两个动作，一个诺言。

normal.en: Commitments in the plural often means a crowded calendar.
normal.cn: 复数形式的承诺，常常意味着排得满满的日程。

normal.en: The doubled t of commit stays in commitment.
normal.cn: commit 的双写 t 在 commitment 里保留下来。

abstract.en: Picture a hand raised in a quiet room to say yes.
abstract.cn: 想象一只在安静的房间里举起的手，说出我愿意。

abstract.en: Picture a runner training on the same track in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者在雨中跑同一条跑道。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar filled with names and dates.
abstract.cn: 想象一本写满人名与日期的日历。

examples.en: She made a commitment to finish the course.
examples.cn: 她承诺要完成这门课程。

examples.en: The job demands real commitment from every member.
examples.cn: 这份工作要求每位成员真正投入。

examples.en: He has too many commitments to travel this month.
examples.cn: 他这个月事务太多，没法出行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 commitment 记成 commit（承诺）加 ment（事情）：承诺下来的那件事，就是你要背起的责任。

root: 由 commit 加名词后缀 -ment 构成，词根上溯拉丁语 committere（托付），本义是被交托下来的事，后指承诺与投入。

sensesIntro.en: From a promise in words, to the effort that keeps it, and finally to the duties it creates.
sensesIntro.cn: 从口头说出的承诺，到维持它的付出，再到它带来的义务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a promise spoken once and never taken back.
core.cn: 核心意象：说出口就不再收回的那句保证。

branches.en: The promise itself is the sense that names the word.
branches.cn: 承诺本身是这个词最直接的义项。

branches.en: Kept promises turn into visible dedication.
branches.cn: 被兑现的承诺会变成看得见的投入。

branches.en: In the plural the word means the duties filling your week.
branches.cn: 用复数时，这个词指填满你一周的那些事务。

branches.en: A promise and the effort behind it are one thing seen twice.
branches.cn: 承诺与它背后的付出，是同一件事的两次显现。

branches.en: Dedication to work and family duties often compete for the same hours.
branches.cn: 对工作的投入与家庭事务常常争夺同样的时间。

intro.en: Commitment is a -ment noun, and it keeps the doubled t of its verb.
intro.cn: commitment 是带 -ment 的名词，并保留了动词双写的 t。

latinIntro.en: The Latin mittere, to send, links commitment with mission and submit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 mittere（送出）把 commitment 与 mission、submit 连在一起。

items.example: Work commitments kept her in the city.
items.exampleCN: 工作上的事务让她留在了城里。

items.example: They commit two days a week to the club.
items.exampleCN: 他们每周为社团投入两天。
她是一位尽心尽力的老师。

items.meaning: the act of promising or giving effort
items.example: Committing to one plan is harder than making ten.
items.exampleCN: 投入一个计划比许下十个愿更难。

items.meaning: the act of sending someone to prison or court
items.example: The committal took place that morning.

items.structure: related noun from the same root
items.meaning: authority or work entrusted to someone
items.example: The commission reported back in June.
items.exampleCN: 委员会六月提交了报告。
